extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for handling, admitting, and processing amendments and replies filed after final rejection or after notice of allowance (including expedited processing and fee requirements) during U.S. patent prosecution under 37 CFR 1.116 and 1.312.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpermanent amendment handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment is nonpermanent (e.g., a paper copy only), applicant is promptly notified that the amendment is not entered and is required to file a permanent copy within 1 month or to order a copy to be made by the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office at his or her expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical entry of the amendment will be made from the permanent copy. If there is no appropriate reply within the 1-month limit, a copy is made by the USPTO, applicant being notified and required to remit the charges or authorize charging them to deposit account or credit card. See MPEP § 509 and MPEP § 608.01 for acceptable copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees when adding claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is required to pay excess claims fees for each claim that is in excess of 3 in independent form or in excess of 20 total (whether dependent or independent); fees for a proper multiple dependent claim are calculated based on the number of claims to which it refers and a separate fee is required in each application containing a proper multiple dependent claim (37 CFR 1.75(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicant adds a new excess claim that is in excess of the number of claims previously paid for (after accounting for canceled claims), applicant must pay the required excess claims fees before the examiner considers the new claim. See MPEP § 607. Example provided for counting independent and total claims when claims are canceled and added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments during interference/reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed during interference proceedings or reexamination are subject to special rules (see Chapter 2300 and relevant CFR sections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter partes and ex parte reexamination practice impose limits (e.g., inter partes reexamination: no amendment other than canceling claims after right of appeal notice, except as provided in § 1.981 or § 41.77(b)(1)). See MPEP Chapter 2300 for detailed procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.116 permissible post-final amendments/evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: After a final rejection or other final action but before or on the same date of filing an appeal, an amendment may (1) cancel claims or comply with form requirements; (2) present rejected claims in better form for consideration on appeal; or (3) touch the merits and be admitted upon a showing of good and sufficient reasons why the amendment is necessary and was not earlier presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits or other evidence filed after final rejection may be admitted upon a showing of good and sufficient reasons (37 CFR 1.116(e)). Admission or refusal does not relieve the proceeding from appeal conditions or abandonment. See 37 CFR 1.116(b),(c),(e) and MPEP § 714.12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on amendments in inter partes reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment other than canceling claims (where cancellation does not affect scope of other pending claims) may be made in an inter partes reexamination proceeding after the right of appeal notice under § 1.953, except as provided in § 1.981 or § 41.77(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar restrictions apply to affidavits/evidence after final in inter partes reexamination. See MPEP § 714.12 and related CFR sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of showing for non-trivial after-final amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where an amendment merely cancels claims, adopts examiner suggestions, removes issues for appeal, or requires only cursory review, compliance with the requirement of a showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b)(3) is expected in all amendments after final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An affidavit or other evidence filed after final may be entered upon showing good and sufficient reasons why the evidence is necessary and was not earlier presented. See 37 CFR 1.116(e); MPEP §§ 1206, 714.13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on further prosecution after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a final rejection that is not premature has been entered, applicant or patent owner no longer has any right to unrestricted further prosecution; however, amendments that place the application in condition for allowance or in better form for appeal may be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments filed after final are not entered as a matter of right; ordinarily not entered unless approved by the examiner. See MPEP § 706.07(f), § 714.13, and § 1206.

rubrics_metrics.name: One personal interview after final action (generally)
rubrics_metrics.description: The prosecution before the examiner should ordinarily be concluded with the final action, but one personal interview by applicant may be entertained after such final action if circumstances warrant; only one request by applicant for a personal interview after final should be granted ordinarily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In exceptional circumstances, a second personal interview may be initiated by the examiner if it would materially assist in placing the application in condition for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim drafting advice to avoid after-final difficulties
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are encouraged to include at filing or no later than the first reply claims varying from the broadest believed allowable to the most detailed they are willing to accept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including a range of claim scope early may alleviate difficulties in prosecution after final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory period timing rule after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant initially replies within 2 months to a final rejection which set a 3-month shortened statutory period and the Office does not mail an advisory action until after the end of the 3-month period, the period for reply for extension-fee calculation purposes will be the date the Office mails the advisory action, but in no event can it extend beyond 6 months from the date of the final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure applies only to a first reply to a final rejection. The exact mandatory wording for the final rejection regarding the shortened statutory period must be included in each final rejection (form paragraphs referenced). Failure to file a reply during the shortened statutory period results in abandonment unless time is extended under 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry not a matter of right after final; permissible replies limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant cannot, as a matter of right, amend any finally rejected claims, add new claims after a final rejection (see 37 CFR 1.116) or reinstate previously canceled claims. A reply under 37 CFR 1.113 is limited to: (A) an amendment complying with 37 CFR 1.116; (B) a Notice of Appeal (and appeal fee); or (C) a request for continued examination (RCE) filed under 37 CFR 1.114 with a submission and fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCE practice under 1.114 does not apply to utility or plant applications filed before June 8, 1995 and design applications. Continued prosecution by CPA applies only to design applications (with limitations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria and reasons for nonentry of after-final amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Refusal to enter a proposed amendment should not be arbitrary. The proposed amendment should be given sufficient consideration to determine whether claims are in condition for allowance and/or whether issues on appeal are simplified. If the amendment raises new matter or new issues requiring further consideration/search, the examiner should identify and explain concisely why entry is refused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of adequate concise reasons for nonentry include: (A) amended claims would not avoid rejections and thus not place the case in condition for allowance or better for appeal; (B) amended claims would raise the issue of new matter; (C) amended claims present new issues requiring further consideration/search; (D) amendment presents additional claims without canceling any finally rejected claims so not placing application in better condition for appeal. Examiner need not always discuss specific deficiencies unless new matter is raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must indicate claim status and appeal-entry expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should indicate the status of each claim of record or proposed in the amendment, and which proposed claims would be entered on the filing of an appeal if filed in a separate paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an amendment is entered for appeal purposes, the examiner must indicate on the advisory action which individual rejection(s) set forth in the action from which the appeal was taken would be used to reject the new or amended claim(s). Use form paragraph 7.169 and PTOL-303 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Action (PTOL-303) use
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Action form PTOL-303 should be used to acknowledge receipt of a reply after final rejection where the reply is prior to filing an appeal brief and does not place the application in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTOL-303 advises applicant of disposition of proposed amendments and the effect of any argument or affidavit not placing the application in condition for allowance or which could not be made allowable by a telephone call to clear up minor matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness goals for examiner response to after-final amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner is expected to turn in a response to an amendment after final rejection within an average of 11 calendar days from receipt by the examiner; a reply to an amendment after final should be mailed within 30 days of receipt by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application is placed in condition for allowance, applicant should be notified promptly by Notice of Allowability (PTOL-37). If delays expected, interview and PTOL-413B Examiner Interview Summary may be used. If no action received within the goal plus normal mailing time for expedited procedure, contact SPE or TC Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment if no appeal or allowable amendment timely filed
rubrics_metrics.description: If no appeal has been filed within the period for reply and no amendment has been submitted to make the application allowable or which can be entered in part, the application stands abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing of a 37 CFR 1.181 petition will not stay the period for reply. See MPEP § 1206 for appeal and post-appeal procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hand-delivery requirements for after-final papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Hand-carried papers for Technology Centers may only be delivered to the USPTO Customer Window (Randolph Building). Effective Dec. 1, 2003, all official patent application related correspondence hand-carried must be delivered to the Customer Window; hand-carried amendments and other replies after final rejection (37 CFR 1.116) will no longer be accepted in the TCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any courier attempting delivery of after-final correspondence at a TC will be re-directed to the Customer Window. Patent application related CDs and other non-paper submissions hand-carried must be delivered to the Customer Window. See MPEP § 502 for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited processing marking and mailing procedure for 37 CFR 1.116 replies
rubrics_metrics.description: To use the expedited procedure for processing amendments and other replies after final rejection under 37 CFR 1.116, the amendment or reply must be marked on the upper right portion 'Reply under 37 CFR 1.116 — Expedited Procedure - Technology Center (Insert Technology Center Number)' and the envelope must be marked 'Mail Stop AF' in the lower left hand corner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Envelope should contain only replies under 37 CFR 1.116 and be mailed to 'Mail Stop AF, Commissioner for Patents, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, Virginia, 22313-1450' or hand-carried to Customer Window. USPTO goal: mail examiner’s action on the reply within 1 month from receipt. Applicant must follow marking to obtain benefits; delays caused by applicant (delayed interviews, petitions) will prevent goal achievement. If no action within goal + normal mailing time, contact SPE then TC Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte Quayle (amendments after allowance) principle
rubrics_metrics.description: After all claims in an application have been allowed the prosecution of the application on the merits is closed even though there may be outstanding formal objections which preclude fully closing the prosecution (Ex parte Quayle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments touching the merits after allowance are treated similarly to amendments after final rejection. Use form paragraph 7.51 (Quayle Action) to require correction of formal matters. See MPEP § 714.14 and § 714.20 for related practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of amendments received after Notice of Allowance (37 CFR 1.312)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment received after the mailing of the notice of allowance has the status of one filed under 37 CFR 1.312. Its entry is a matter of grace and any amendment under 1.312 must be filed before or with payment of the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the amendment is filed prior to mailing but received by the examiner after mailing, it may also not be approved for entry. If approved, examiner may enter the amendment and provide a supplemental notice of allowance, or withdraw the application from issue and provide an Office action. If the application was closed to further amendment by the prior Office action, the application will not be withdrawn from issue for entry of an amendment that would reopen prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of 'amendment' under 37 CFR 1.312
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'amendment' broadly encompasses any change in the file record after allowance, including amendments to the specification, drawings, claims; changes in inventorship; submission of prior art; petitions to correct spelling or change order of inventors, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment under 1.312 must comply with 37 CFR 1.121 and be filed on or before the date the issue fee is paid (except where required by Office of Data Management). The supervisory patent examiner approves recommendations under 1.312. Supplemental reissue oaths/declarations are treated as amendments under 1.312; supplemental oaths/declarations (non-reissue) are not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for amendments under 1.312 that affect claims or disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: For amendments affecting disclosure, scope of any claim, or adding a claim under 1.312, the remarks accompanying the amendment must fully and clearly state: (A) why the amendment is needed; (B) why the proposed amended or new claims require no additional search or examination; (C) why the claims are patentable; and (D) why they were not presented earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirements of 37 CFR 1.111(c) with respect to pointing out patentable novelty of any claim sought to be added or amended apply to 1.312 amendments as in ordinary amendments. See MPEP §§ 713.04, 713.10 and 714.16.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.312 not a vehicle for continued prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.312 was never intended to provide a way for continued prosecution after an application has been passed for issue; consideration under 1.312 cannot be demanded as a matter of right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recommending non-entry, a detailed statement of reasons is not necessary; a simple statement that the proposed claim is not obviously allowable and brief reason why is usually adequate. Sufficient reasons for nonentry include (A) additional search required; (B) more than cursory review of the record necessary; (C) amendment would involve materially added work on the Office. See MPEP § 714.16(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee requirements for 1.312 amendments adding claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 adds claims (total and independent) in excess of the number previously paid for, additional fees are required; the amendment is not considered by the examiner unless accompanied by the full fee required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 607 and 35 U.S.C. 41 for fee computation and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: No amendments after payment of issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendments should be filed after the date the issue fee has been paid; 37 CFR 1.312 no longer permits filing an amendment after the date the issue fee was paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 13.10 'Amendment Filed After the Payment of Issue Fee, Not Entered' to notify applicant when amendment was filed after issue fee date. See MPEP § 714.16(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of copied patent claims filed after allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment received after notice of allowance includes one or more claims copied or substantially copied from a patent, special procedure applies (see Chapter 2300). The entry of copied patent claims is not a matter of right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP Chapter 2300 for the procedure to be followed and MPEP §§ 607 and 714.16(c) for fee requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing/processing of 1.312 amendments affecting disclosure after allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments under 37 CFR 1.312 affecting the disclosure, adding claims, or changing claim scope are sent by OPAP to Publishing Division which forwards the proposed amendment, file, and drawing (if any) to the Technology Center which allowed the application; for IFW applications OPAP Central Scanning scans and messages Data Management and the TC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hand-delivered amendments under 1.312 are no longer accepted in the TC (unless required by Office of Data Management) and must be delivered to the Customer Window. If the application has been reclassified to another TC after allowance, the proposed amendment and file are transmitted to that TC.
